subject: science
passage: Yala National Park, in the dry southeastern corner of Sri Lanka, is thought to have one of the highest densities of leopards anywhere in the world. Visitors who hope to see one have several things on their side, such ______ the park's open scrubland, its many watering holes, and the habit of the Sri Lankan leopard, which has no tigers or lions to compete with, of hunting by day as well as by night. Even so, a sighting is never guaranteed, and guides like to say that the leopard decides when it will be seen.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Such as" introduces the examples that follow, and the examples complete the phrase. No punctuation should separate "such as" from the items it introduces.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma can't separate "such as" from the examples that complete it.
explanation.B: Correct. "Such as" leads directly into its examples with no punctuation between them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides; the list of examples is not a clause.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause; it can't come between "such as" and the examples it introduces.
